newsitem.title: JAPAN: Shareholder sues Sumitomo over copper loss fund.
newsitem.headline: Shareholder sues Sumitomo over copper loss fund.

text.p: A Sumitomo Corp shareholder filed a lawsuit on Thursday aimed at stopping the trading house from setting up a special fund to pay for its massive copper trading losses.
The shareholders' meeting was held on June 27, only two weeks after Sumitomo announced it had amassed huge losses from unauthorised copper trades over a 10-year period.
The suit contends that the vote to set up the fund and cancel a share buyback scheme was taken improperly.

Several of those attending the meeting have complained they were shunted into side rooms to watch the proceedings on television monitors, with no chance to question executives, while the main room was filled with Sumitomo employees who had arrived early.

The shareholders' meeting lasted less than 40 minutes. It approved by voice vote, with no casting of ballots, the company's plans to cover the massive copper losses by setting up a separate fund and by cancelling a share buy-back.

"I thought it was strange that the shareholders' meeting ended without any objections, despite the occurrence of such a major incident," Kazuyoshi Yuoka, who filed the suit, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Yuoka said he had been sitting in the main room where the meeting was being held.

He said: "I was so frustrated with Sumitomo's undemocratic way of conducting the shareholders' meeting. Although I raised my hand, the Sumitomo side did not allow me to ask detailed questions on copper trading losses."
"The shareholders' meeting was well prepared and just a ceremony for the Sumitomo management," Yuoka said.
A team of 10 lawyers is involved in Yuoka's lawsuit against Sumitomo.

"Yuoka is not necessarily opposed to the special fund, but is opposed to the fact that it was neither discussed nor debated," one of the lawyers told Reuters. "He is also opposed to the fact that the company did not reveal the extent of the retirement payments."

A Sumitomo spokesman said the suit filed on Thursday at a district court in Osaka -- the western Japanese city where Sumitomo is based -- sought to repeal approval of the fund and of retirement payments to five members of the board of directors.

Sumitomo said in a statement: "If this case is requesting the repeal of resolutions at our general shareholders' meeting, it is our belief that the meeting was held for the shareholders themselves and that procedurally it was in accord with commercial law, and therefore there are no problems with it."

Sumitomo jumped back into the headlines last week when, after months of official silence on the copper scandal, it announced that it had raised its estimate of the copper trading losses to $2.6 billion from the $1.8 billion it announced in June.
